topic: How AI Models Become Assistants: Pre-Training to Post-Training
description: Check your understanding of Common Crawl, FineWeb, base models, SFT, instruction tuning, RLHF, reward hacking, and why post-training shapes behaviour.

questions.question: What are the three main steps to turn a base predictor into a public chat assistant?
options: Tokenization, embeddings, and attention
Pre-training, training, and post-training
Crawling, advertising, and API billing
questions.explanation: The notes frame ChatGPT-style assistants as: (1) pre-training data, (2) training the base model, (3) post-training so it behaves like a public assistant.

questions.question: What is Common Crawl?
options: OpenAI's private chat logs used only for GPT-4
A non-profit open archive of web crawl data used as a major LLM data source
A Hugging Face tool that writes system prompts
questions.explanation: Common Crawl maintains a free public snapshot of the internet (hundreds of billions of pages) that researchers and companies can use for training.

questions.question: Why can't companies just feed raw HTML into an LLM for training?
options: HTML is already the perfect training format
Models need refined useful text, not menus, junk, private or adult content
HTML files are too small to matter
questions.explanation: Raw pages include navigation and unwanted content. Data must be refined/filtered into clean text before training.

questions.question: What is FineWeb?
options: A video dataset of Fine-tuned Webcams
Hugging Face's cleaned Common Crawl collection (~15 trillion tokens) for pre-training
The name of ChatGPT's reward model
questions.explanation: FineWeb is processed Common Crawl: spam/repetition/low quality removed. FineWeb-Edu is a smaller educational-only slice.

questions.question: What is the result of the Training step (step 2)?
options: A public ChatGPT product with tools and memory
A Base / foundation model that predicts next tokens but is not yet a helpful assistant
Only a Reward Model
questions.explanation: Clean data + the training loop (Transformer, loss, backprop) produces a base model — still not ready for the public.

questions.question: How is a base model different from a tuned assistant?
options: They are identical; marketing names differ
A base model is a general next-token student; a tuned model is specialized to follow instructions and behave well
A base model cannot predict tokens at all
questions.explanation: Analogy in the notes: base = college graduate; tuned = same person after job-specific training for tone, structure, humility.

questions.question: What does Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) do?
options: It invents a brand-new learning algorithm unrelated to loss
It continues training on targeted Q&A/chat examples so the model follows instructions
It only crawls FineWeb
questions.explanation: SFT uses the same loop (predict → loss → backward → update) on a smaller, targeted dataset. Result: SFT Model.

questions.question: What is instruction tuning mainly for?
options: Teaching the model to complete 'The sky is...' only
Teaching the model to follow human commands (explain, JSON, poem, classify) not just next-word completion
Replacing GPUs with CPUs
questions.explanation: Instruction tuning turns a raw completer into an assistant that can handle direct prompts and requested formats.

questions.question: Why can Claude feel better at debugging than another model?
options: All post-base models are trained on identical data
After the base model, datasets and fine/instruction-tuning give each company a different 'taste'
Debugging skill is only from the system prompt color
questions.explanation: Most personality/skill flavor happens after the base model via different data and tuning (e.g. lots of debugging examples).

questions.question: What does the System role do in a conversation?
options: It is the user's latest question
It is the hidden rulebook for personality, tone, and boundaries — usually highest priority
It is only used to store past assistant replies
questions.explanation: SYSTEM vs USER vs ASSISTANT separate developer rules, human input, and model replies. System instructions should not be ignored.

questions.question: Why is SFT not always enough?
options: It already solves all human preference and reasoning issues
It teaches style/format but struggles with deep reasoning, changing facts, and which answer humans prefer
It cannot run on GPUs
questions.explanation: Users want short vs long vs technical answers. SFT doesn't fully capture that taste — human preference / RLHF comes next.

questions.question: What is the Evaluation Gap?
options: The gap between HTTP and HTTPS
It's easier to judge which answer is better than to write the ideal answer from scratch
The gap between CPU and GPU price
questions.explanation: You can pick the funnier joke more easily than invent one. Generators create; discriminators/evaluators judge — evaluation is still hard and expensive.

questions.question: What is a Reward Model?
options: The Common Crawl bot
A model trained on human preference comparisons that scores answers for helpfulness/safety/quality
The user's ChatGPT Plus invoice
questions.explanation: Millions of A vs B rankings train a digital judge. ChatGPT's 'which response do you prefer?' is the same idea.

questions.question: How does RLHF work at a high level?
options: The model crawls FineWeb again from scratch
The AI proposes answers, humans (or a reward model) rank them, then RL makes high-preference styles more likely
RLHF only deletes adult URLs
questions.explanation: Three beats: generate choices → humans grade → learn from the reward. Core technique behind ChatGPT/Claude-style assistants.

questions.question: What is reward hacking?
options: Getting a high measured score without doing the real intended job
Paying humans more to label faster
Using more GPUs during pre-training
questions.explanation: Like a student flipping 500 flashcards for an A+ without learning. The metric is gamed; the goal is missed.

questions.question: What does Goodhart’s Law / reward over-optimization warn?
options: A higher reward score always means more usefulness
Once a metric becomes the target, it can stop being a good measure — usefulness can stall or drop
System prompts must be written in JSON only
questions.explanation: Chase the number too hard and the model finds shortcuts that please the scorer, not the user. Helpful ≠ always agreeing.

questions.question: Training vs post-training — which is right?
options: Training builds capabilities; post-training mainly shapes how those capabilities are expressed
Post-training always re-teaches every fact from scratch (e.g. closures)
They are the same step with two names
questions.explanation: Knowing JS closures may already be in the capability base. Post-training teaches expressing it as a clear assistant answer.
